title: Vendor Onramp: Redwood parity mapping — Skyline Health demo
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Skyline Health through mapping common OpenAI/Anthropic/Together API usage to Redwood endpoints, demoed Console optimizations, discussed PHI constraints and private deployment options. Action items: benchmark plan, security pack, pricing estimate for pilot. Several clarifying questions on deterministic responses, embeddings dimensional parity, and KMS/SSO were raised.
action_items: Ravi: share initial benchmark spreadsheet and sample cURL parity conversions by 2025-12-11
Jamie: send Dedicated and Private pricing sheet and pilot SLAs by 2025-12-10
Leah: schedule security follow-up with compliance docs attached by 2025-12-12
next_steps: Run a 2-week pilot on a small embedding index (10k docs) using the Redwood hosted API + caching suggestions
Redwood to provide a quickstart repo with sample mapping of OpenAI Chat/completions + Anthropic to Redwood equivalents
Customer to confirm pilot scope and PHI redaction approach
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-08
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Leah Torres (Redwood CSM); Dr. Anika Bose, Marco Reyes, Sophie Liu, Tom H. (Skyline)

Auto-generated summary (may be fuzzy): Redwood parity demo for migrating from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together. Discussed embeddings, function-calling, private deployment options and security.

Topics: 1) API parity mapping 2) Embedding parity and reranking 3) Console Optimize tips 4) Private deployment and KMS 5) Next steps and benchmarks

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Jamie Park from Redwood, Ravi on the call, Leah is here too.
[00:08] Anika: Hi, thanks. I'm Anika, head of ML at Skyline. We have Marco, Sophie, Tom on. Appreciate you fitting this in.
[00:15] Jamie: For context, we're doing a vendor onramp — you mentioned currently prototyping with OpenAI and Anthropic and looking at how to port to Redwood with parity. We'll demo the API mapping, console, and Optimize recommendations. Any must-ask items before we start?
[00:30] Anika: Main things — embeddings parity for our search index, how function calling maps over, and whether we can keep latency SLOs. Also PHI concerns — we need private deployment options.
[00:40] Ravi: Great, we'll hit those. Quick note — some of the terms might come through weird in the transcript, e.g., KV cash instead of KV cache, sorry in advance.
[00:50] Marco: Also curious about tokenization differences and if output determinism changes.
[01:00] Jamie: Good call out. We'll show endpoint-level examples: completions/chat mapping, then embeddings + reranking patterns, and then Console Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization.

--- Demo start ---

[05:15] Ravi: Alright, I'm sharing my screen. First slide is a simple mapping table — OpenAI ChatCompletion -> Redwood /v1/chat.generate; Anthropic Convo -> Redwood conversational endpoint, and Together's streaming semantics map to Redwood streaming with delta tokens. Note: exact param names differ e.g., "temperature" is shared, but we also have explicit "response_format" for structured outputs.
[05:50] Anika: Can you show a real cURL example?
[05:55] Ravi: Yep. Here's a three-line cURL that swaps the model name and a small prompt. (typing noises) For Anthropic to Redwood mapping: where Anthropic uses "instructions", we map to system messages in chat and adjust stop sequences. Example output — you should see similar tokens.
[06:30] Marco: I'm seeing slightly different token counts in the demo, is that normal?
[06:35] Ravi: It can vary because of tokenizers; we provide a tokenizer helper in the SDK to align counts. For embeddings, model dimensionality is important — we have embeddings with 1536 dims and 1024 dims depending on model family which you'd map to your vector index schema.
[07:05] Sophie: Our question is about PHI and retention. If we use hosted API, does Redwood persist logs?
[07:12] Jamie: Hosted keeps transient logs for X hours by default, and we have dedicated/private deployments for no retention. We'll attach the security pack with SOC2/ISO notes and KMS integrations.
[07:22] Sophie: We need HIPA— HIPAA-adjacent controls.
[07:25] Leah: We do have customers operating under PHI constraints using Redwood Private with a customer-controlled VPC and KMS/HSM; we'll share a case study.

[08:00] Ravi: Back to parity — here's a live snippet converting an OpenAI chat request with function calling to Redwood's function schema. Note, Redwood supports structured function results and automatic schema validation. In practice you'd replace the function name and payload keys but keep call semantics. (background typing)
[09:10] Tom: Do you guarantee the same function calling determinism? If the helper returns different json shapes that's risky.
[09:20] Ravi: Determinism can vary by model. On the platform side we support alpha rollouts and pinned versions. For pilot, we recommend pinning a model and using Redwood Optimize to run a set of eval prompts to check for output regression. We can also do automatic fallback to a more deterministic model variant.

[11:30] Marco: What about embeddings drift over time if models are updated? We've seen differences post-version bumps with other vendors.
[11:40] Jamie: Good point. Redwood supports model version pinning at the account or route level and we surface embedding quality comparisons in the Console. We'll include a sample script to run embedding parity checks against a test corpus.

[13:05] Ravi: Now profiling latency — here's our Console trace for a production route: token-level breakdown, KV cache hit rate, batching windows. Note: the example shows a 95th percentile latency of ~120ms for short prompts on a dedicated pool. If you go hosted with caching it's similar but depends on concurrency.
[13:40] Anika: How does caching affect hallucinations?
[13:45] Ravi: Caching prefixes and KV cache reduce cost and latency for repeated patterns but you should design caches carefully for PHI — e.g., don't cache raw inputs containing PHI unless redaction's applied.

[15:00] Sophie: On private deployment — we want customer's control plane in our VPC, SAML SSO, and KMS key control. Is that supported?
[15:10] Jamie: Yes — Redwood Private offers a customer-managed control plane, SSO via SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. We'll include the runbook and network diagram.

[16:30] Ravi: Let's switch to embeddings demo. Indexed 10k docs in Pinecone in the demo; we show how to swap the vector insert calls to Redwood's embedding endpoint. The SDK shim is two lines — create_embedding(model: "redwood-embedding-1", text: ...). Then we re-run the nearest-neighbor queries.
[17:05] Marco: Our current index schema uses 1536 dims. If Redwood embedding dims differ, will our existing Pinecone index break?
[17:12] Ravi: If dims differ you need to re-index. That's why parity mapping includes model choice recommendations. For compatibility we recommend picking a Redwood embedding model that matches your existing dimensionality or reindexing as part of the pilot. We'll help size compute and cost for reindexing.

[19:00] Jamie: Quick interjection — there's a common question on billing: host vs dedicated. For pilot, hosted with usage billing is quickest. Dedicated makes sense at scale for predictability. We'll include a cost estimate.
[19:20] Tom: Any examples of batching settings for a low-latency product?
[19:25] Ravi: Yes, Optimize suggests batching windows of 10-30ms for interactive flows or larger for background jobs; it also suggests dynamic batching thresholds based on 99p latency SLOs.

[22:10] Marco: Can you show the Console rollout UI?
[22:15] Ravi: (screen share) Here's the rollout panel — you can do canary percentages, A/Bs with different models, automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to eval sets. You can also attach a prompt set; if quality drops below a threshold it alerts and may auto-fallback.
[23:00] Anika: Nice. We would want to surface regression alerts to PagerDuty.
[23:05] Leah: We have webhooks and integrations to push alerts into PagerDuty or Slack.

[25:40] Sophie: For compliance we need audit logs of query payloads (redacted) and admin actions.
[25:45] Jamie: Audit logs are available in Private and Dedicated with retention windows you control; hosted has standard logs but we can do extended retention as an add-on.

[28:00] Ravi: Ok moving toward a concrete pilot proposal — 2-week pilot: 10k doc embedding index, reranking integration in your search flow, and a small set of chat prompts mapped from OpenAI. We'll run parity checks and provide a benchmark report.
[28:30] Anika: That fits our timeline, we want the pilot started in January. Who owns infra during pilot?
[28:40] Jamie: Redwood can run the hosted pilot; if you need Private we'll scope a quick Private PoC. Usually infra ownership during hosted pilots is minimal on your side.

[30:10] Marco: A couple of nitty-gritty items — how are rate limits enforced? We have spiky traffic from nightly batches.
[30:20] Ravi: We have per-route quotas and token-based rate limits; for spiky workloads we recommend a dedicated pool with autoscaling and burst capacity. We'll include recommended autoscale policies based on your concurrency shape.

[33:00] Tom: Are there known incompatibilities when porting Together.ai streams to Redwood? We rely on streaming deltas for UI.
[33:10] Ravi: Redwood supports server-sent events and streaming delta tokens; semantics are similar but you may need to adapt the client to Redwood streaming events. We'll provide a sample client shim that matches Together's event keys.

[36:50] Sophie: Security question — do you support customer-managed encryption keys for hosted?
[36:55] Jamie: Hosted supports bring-your-own-key via KMS integration for certain enterprise tiers; Private gives you full KMS control. We'll provide the KMS integration doc.

[39:00] Marco: For embeddings performance, can we get a small benchmark that shows p99 for nearest neighbor queries end-to-end?
[39:08] Ravi: Yes, we'll run a benchmark with your index size and provide latency + cost breakdown. We'll include token-level profiling for generation flows and vector insert/query timings.

[41:20] Anika: On evaluation, how do you measure semantic parity? We care about MRR and human evals.
[41:30] Ravi: We recommend a hybrid approach — automated metrics (MRR, recall@k) plus a small human eval set for sensitive cases. Console can store eval runs and trend them over time.

[44:00] Jamie: Wrapping up — key deliverables we'll send: security pack + KMS runbook, benchmark spreadsheet, quickstart repo with example conversions (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood), pricing for pilot.
[44:15] Leah: And I'll set up the security follow-up with Sophie next Friday.
[44:20] Sophie: Works for me.

[45:30] Tom: A couple of final questions — if the pilot shows parity regressions, do you offer remediation assistance?
[45:40] Jamie: Yes, our Solutions Engineering and Research teams will work with you to tweak prompts, recommend model variants and quantization profiles; if it's model-level we can suggest different family or version pins.

[49:00] Marco: Any gotchas about cost when switching embedding models?
[49:10] Ravi: Main cost drivers are token generation and embedding unit price; reindexing one-off cost and host vs dedicated compute matter. Optimize will give you an estimated cost per 1M tokens and per-embedding for the selected model.

[51:50] Jamie: Final recap: Pilot scope agreed in principle — 2 weeks, 10k docs, parity checks on embedding dims and chat function calling. Action items will be in the follow-up email.
[52:10] Anika: Great, thanks all. We look forward to the quickstart.
[52:20] Jamie: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and the docs.
[52:25] (meeting ends)
questions: Can Redwood match embedding dimensionality to avoid reindexing?
How are function-calling JSON schemas validated and kept deterministic?
What are the PHI retention options for hosted vs private?
